ambiguity_traps: A fluent specific error would invent facts.
permitted_rewrites: Use direct language without adding technical detail.
Report missing operation, input, cause, and actionable recovery.
prohibited_inventions: An operation name, input name, cause, status code, or successful retry promise.
source_facts: The source suggests checking an unspecified item and retrying.
The source provides no cause or affected resource.

checks.name: reports_unknown_cause
checks.value: (?i)(?:cause|reason)[^.;]{0,50}(?:unknown|not known|unspecified|unclear|undetermined|not provided|not stated|not given|not identified|not specified)|(?:unknown|not known|unspecified|unclear|undetermined|not provided|not stated|not given|not identified|not specified)[^.;]{0,50}(?:cause|reason)

judge_criteria: Score technical fidelity from 0 to 4; any invented operation, cause, or resource is critical.
Score residual ambiguity and actionability from 0 to 4 while recognizing the source limit.
Score readability, profile compliance, unnecessary edits, and source traceability from 0 to 4.
observable_success: Does not invent missing technical facts
Reports why the error cannot become fully actionable
Retains retry as the only stated next action
prohibited_outcomes: Invents a file, request, server, cause, or status code
prompt: Rewrite this user-facing error with the engineering-default SEE profile. Source: Something went wrong. Check the thing and try again. Retain the instruction to try again. Do not invent the operation, input, cause, or recovery outcome. Respond with exactly three newline-separated fields: PROFILE: strict|engineering-default; REWRITE: <one line>; AMBIGUITIES: <text or none>.

ambiguity_traps: Do not treat the absence of SHALL on a descriptive fact as an ambiguity.
conditions_and_exceptions: The code-247 obligation applies when the Orin gateway receives a Bex request.
permitted_rewrites: Split the obligation and descriptive relations into separate statements.
Use active or passive voice without changing force or roles.
prohibited_inventions: Another obligation, header, transport, exception, or nonce source.
required_structure: Keep the keyword convention, obligation, and descriptive copy fact distinct.
source_facts: Receipt of a Bex request triggers the code-247 obligation.
The request carries a nonce that the gateway copies into X-Orin-Nonce as a descriptive fact.

checks.name: descriptive_copy_fact
checks.value: (?is)^(?!.*(?:SHALL|MUST|SHOULD|MAY)\s+(?:copy|place).*?(?:nonce|X-Orin-Nonce))(?!.*(?:nonce|X-Orin-Nonce).*?(?:SHALL|MUST|SHOULD|MAY)\s+be\s+(?:copied|placed)).*(?:gateway copies (?:that nonce|the client nonce) into (?:the )?(?:response header X-Orin-Nonce|X-Orin-Nonce response header)|(?:that nonce|the client nonce) is copied by the gateway into (?:the )?(?:response header X-Orin-Nonce|X-Orin-Nonce response header))

judge_criteria: A declared keyword convention does not convert adjacent descriptive facts into obligations.
Reject any added obligation keyword on the nonce-copy relation.
Preserve request, gateway, nonce, and header roles.
observable_success: Keeps the nonce-copy relation descriptive and reports no ambiguity.
prohibited_outcomes: [response_obligation] Weakens or negates the code-247 obligation.
[descriptive_copy_fact] Adds SHALL, MUST, SHOULD, or MAY to the nonce-copy fact or reverses its roles.
[clear_source] Reports the descriptive fact as an unresolved obligation ambiguity.
prompt: Rewrite this interface contract with the engineering-default SEE profile. The contract declares that SHALL means mandatory. Preserve the SHALL response obligation, but keep the separate nonce-copy statement as a descriptive fact. Do not add an obligation keyword to that fact. Source: SHALL means mandatory. When the Orin gateway receives a Bex request, it SHALL return code 247. The request carries a client nonce. The gateway copies that nonce into response header X-Orin-Nonce. Respond with exactly three newline-separated fields: PROFILE: strict|engineering-default; REWRITE: <one line>; AMBIGUITIES: <text or none>.

conditions_and_exceptions: Only the header value is authorized for replacement.
permitted_rewrites: Reorder the report and authorization sentences without changing attribution or authorization.
prohibited_inventions: Another reporter, authorization, redaction target, or incident fact.
protected_spans: Security authorizes replacing only the header value with [REDACTED-AUTHORIZED].
required_structure: Keep the analyst report distinct from the authorization.
source_facts: Ivo reported that the request header and secret value were present.
Security currently authorizes redaction of only the header value.

judge_criteria: Authorization tense and exclusive scope are security-consequential.
Only the secret value may change.
Reject a historical authorization or broader redaction.
observable_success: Removes the secret and retains the header name and analyst attribution.
Preserves current authorization and its exclusive scope exactly.
prohibited_outcomes: [authorization_scope] Changes authorizes to authorized or removes only.
[clear_source] Reports an ambiguity not present in the source.
prompt: Rewrite this security incident note with the engineering-default SEE profile. Redact only the secret value. Preserve this authorization sentence byte-for-byte: Security authorizes replacing only the header value with [REDACTED-AUTHORIZED]. Source: Analyst Ivo reported that request header X-Maple-Key: 4cf9-lark-ember was present. Security authorizes replacing only the header value with [REDACTED-AUTHORIZED]. Respond with exactly three newline-separated fields: PROFILE: strict|engineering-default; REWRITE: <one line>; AMBIGUITIES: <text or none>.
